title: Length of a Degree of Latitude

blocks.content: Because the Earth is an oblate spheroid, a degree of latitude is slightly longer at the poles than at the equator.

rows: Greater curvature due to equatorial bulge
Flatter curvature due to polar flattening

items: Exam Trap: Students often incorrectly assume latitude degrees are longer at the equator; in fact, 1° of latitude is longest near the poles due to flattening.
Standard Conversion: For numerical problems, 1 degree of latitude is standardly approximated as 111 km (or 60 nautical miles).
Key Definition: 1 nautical mile equals 1 minute (1/60th of a degree) of latitude along a meridian.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The average linear distance for one degree of latitude is approximately 111 kilometers (69 miles).
Earth's shape is an oblate spheroid—flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator.
Due to this polar flattening, the curvature of the Earth is flatter near the poles, making a degree of latitude slightly longer at the poles (111.69 km) than at the equator (110.56 km).
Parallels of latitude are concentric circles that remain equidistant from one another everywhere on the globe.
